questions.question: If a + b - c = 5 and ab - bc - ac = 10, then find the value of a² + b² + c².
questions.solution:
**Given:**

a + b - c = 5 and ab - bc - ac = 10

**Concept used:**

(a + b - c)2 = a2 + b2 + c2 + 2ab - 2bc - 2ac

**Calculation:**

(a + b - c)2 = a2 + b2 + c2 + 2ab - 2bc - 2ac

⇒ (5)² = a2 + b2 + c2 + 2(ab - bc - ac)

⇒ 25 = a2 + b2 + c2 + 2 × 10

⇒ a2 + b2 + c2 = 25 - 20

⇒ a2 + b2 + c2 = 5

**∴ The value of a2 + b2 + c2 is 5.**

questions.question: The sum of three numbers is 98. If the ratio of the first to the second is 2 : 3 and that of the second to the third is 5 : 8, then the third number is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Sum of three numbers = 98.

Ratio of First number to Second number is 2 : 3.

Ratio of Second number to Third number is 5 : 8.

**Calculation:**

Let the three numbers be A, B and C.

Then,

A : B = 2 : 3 ----(i)

B : C = 5 : 8 ----(ii)

Multiplying eq (i) by 5 and eq (ii) by 3 we get

A : B : C = 10 : 15 : 24

Now C = 98 × 24/49

⇒ C = 48 

**∴ The third number is 48.**

questions.question: In a ΔABC, the bisector of ∠A meets BC at D. If AB = 9.6 cm, AC = 11.2 cm and BD = 4.8 cm, the perimeter (in cm) of ΔABC is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

AB = 9.6 cm

AC = 11.2 cm

BD = 4.8 cm

**Concept used:**

Angle bisector theorem = The angle bisector of any angle will divide the opposite side in the ratio of the sides containing the angle.

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e89573a74bef41851a8020a3784f8f91389953834d37e7ed4f698350c3b0ad46.png] 

According to the concept,

BD/CD = AB/AC

⇒ 4.8/CD = 9.6/11.2

⇒ 1/CD = 2/11.2

⇒ CD = 5.6

So, BC = 4.8 + 5.6

⇒ BC = 10.4

Now,

Perimeter of ΔABC = 9.6 + 10.4 + 11.2

⇒ 31.2 cm

**∴ The perimeter (in cm) of ΔABC is 31.2.**

questions.question: The price of an item is reduced by 20%. As a result, customers can get 2 kg more of it for ₹360. Find the original price (in ₹) per kg of the item.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The price of an item is reduced by 20%. As a result, customers can get 2 kg more of it for ₹360

**Calculation:**

20% = 1/5

Let the actual price be 5x

So, after reduction it will be 4x

According to the question,

(360/4x) - (360/5x) = 2

⇒ (90/x) - (72/x) = 2

⇒ [(90 - 72)/x] = 2

⇒ 18 = 2x

⇒ x = 9

So, actual price = 5 × 9 = 45

**∴ The original price (in ₹) per kg of the item is 45.**

questions.question: What is the amount (in ₹) of a sum of ₹32,000 at 20% per annum for 9 months, compounded quarterly?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Sum = Rs. 32000

Rate = 20%

Time = 9 month

**Concept used:**

The formula for quarterly compound interest

 A = P(1 + (frac{r)/(4)}{100})^(4t)/(12)

A = amount

P = principal or sum

r = rate of interest

t = time

**Calculation:**

Interest rate for quarterly = 20/4 = 5%

Time = 4 × 9/12 = 3

So,

A = 32000(1 + 5/100)³

⇒ A = 32000(21/20)3

⇒ A = 32000 × (9261/8000)

⇒ A = 37044

**∴ Required amount is Rs. 37044.**

questions.question: Shyam drives his car 30 km at a speed of 45 km/h and, for the next 1 h 20 m, he drives it at a speed of 51 km/h. Find his average speed (in km/h) for the entire journey.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Shyam drives his car 30 km at a speed of 45 km/h and, for the next 1 h 20 m, he drives it at a speed of 51 km/h.

**Concept used:**

Average speed = Total distance/total time

**Calculation:**

Shyam can go 45 km in 60 min

So, he can go 3 km in 4 min

again, he can go 30 km in 40 min

For next 1 h and 20 min he drived at a speed of 51 km/h

Now, 1 h and 20 min = 4/3 hours [∵ 1 hour = 60 min]

Now,

In 4/3 hours he will go 51 × 4/3 = 68 km

Total distance = 68 + 30 = 98 km

Total time = 40 min + 1 hour 20 min = 2 hours

Average speed = 98/2

⇒ 49 km/h

**∴ His average speed (in km/h) for the entire journey was 49.**

questions.question: A shopkeeper allows a 28% discount on the marked price of an article and still makes a profit of 30%. If he gains ₹39.90 on the sale of one article, then what is the marked price (to the nearest ₹) of the article?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Discount % = 28

Profit% = 30

Gain = Rs. 39.90

**Concept used:**

Selling price = Cost price + cost price × profit%

Selling price = Marked price - marked price × discount%

**Calculation:**

Gain amount = 39.90

According to the question, 30% of the CP of the article = 39.90

⇒ 10% of the CP of the article = 13.30

⇒ 100% of the CP of the article = 133 i.e cost price

⇒ 130% of the CP of the article = 172.9 i.e selling price

Now,

172.9 = Marked price - Marked price × 28%

⇒ 172.9 = Marked price - 0.28.Marked price

⇒ 172.9 = 0.72.Marked price

⇒ 172.9/0.72 = Marked price

⇒ Marked price = 240.133 ≈ 240

**∴ The marked price (to the nearest ₹) of the article is 240.**

questions.question: A man, a woman and a boy can complete a work in 3, 4 and 12 days, respectively. How many boys must assist one man and one woman to complete the same work in one day?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A man, a woman, and a boy can complete a work in 3, 4, and 12 days

**Concept used:**

Efficiency = Total work/time taken

For this type of question, we take LCM of time taken by the individual people.

**Calculation:**

LCM of 3, 4, and 12 is 12

Let the total work be 12 units

So, efficiency of a man = 12/3 = 4 units/ day

Efficiency of a woman = 12/4 = 3 units/ day

Efficiency of a boy = 12/12 = 1 units/ day

To complete the whole work in one day the effective efficiency must be 12

So, effective efficiency of a man and woman = 4 + 3 = 7 units

Now, remaining = 12 - 7 = 5

So, number of boys = 5/1 = 5

**∴ 5 boys must assist one man and one woman to complete the same work in one day.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**Man's 1 day work = 1/3

Woman's 1 day work = 1/4

Boy's 1 day work = 1/12

According to question-

⇒ 1 × (1/3) + 1 × (1/4) + x × (1/12) = 1 { ∵ x be the no. of boys needed} 

⇒ x/12 = 1 - (1/3) - (1/4)

⇒ x/12 = (12 - 7)/12

⇒ x = 5

∴ **5 Boys are needed to complete the work.**

questions.question: Two poles of heights 10 m and 17 m are fixed to a level ground. The distance between the bottom of the poles is 24 m. What is the distance (in m) between their tops?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Two poles of heights 10 m and 17 m are fixed to level ground.

The distance between the bottom of the poles is 24 m

**Concept used:**

Hypotenuse² = Perpendicular² + Base² 

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e8600e18f3418fb31191fbbd34ca6ba010850980ac7cf11f6120156af2daf06b.png] 

Let AB be 10 m and CD be 17 m 

AP = BD = 24 m

AB = PD = 10 m

So, CP = 7 m

Applying pythagoras theorem in ΔACP

AC² = AP² + CP²

⇒ AC2 = 242 + 72

⇒ AC2 = 576 + 49

⇒ AC2 = 625

⇒ AC = 25

**∴ The distance (in m) between their tops is 25.**
